items: Constructor: Constructor is a special type of function which is used to initialize the class variables. In Python the __init__() method is used to initialize an object's properties when it is created.

blocks.text: class Car: def __init__(self , color): self . color = color
book_errors: class Car: def __init__(self , color): self . color = color

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The constructor example is printed on one line, which is a SyntaxError (a def cannot follow class Car: on the same line). Written out: class Car:, then def __init__(self , color): indented, then self.color = color indented once more.

items: Destructor: The __del__() method is called when an object is deleted. It is used for cleanup purposes.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The message string has no opening quote (self.color ,  is being deleted . ")), a SyntaxError. It should be print("Car with color", self.color, "is being deleted.").
The destructor here prints a message when the object is deleted, indicating cleanup.
Explanation: The 'Car' class initializes with a 'color' attribute and prints a message when an instance is deleted, indicating the car with the given color is being removed.
